Wine guides

Practical, sourced guides to ordering wine in restaurants, from the makers of PocSomm.

How much do restaurants mark up wine? US restaurants typically charge about 3 times what they paid for a bottle, roughly 2 times the shop price. UK lists average about 3 times retail. Wine by the glass carries the biggest markup. Sources and a free calculator. How to tell if a wine on a restaurant list is good value Divide the list price by what the same bottle costs in a shop. 1.75 times or less is great value, up to 3 times is fair, more is a high markup. How to find the shop price, and when the rule bends. How to choose wine from a restaurant wine list Set a budget, decide glass or bottle, match the wine to the food, then pick the best value in that range and let the sommelier help. A practical guide with the numbers behind it. Wine markup calculator Free wine markup calculator. Enter the restaurant price and the shop price of a bottle (or a glass) to see the markup and whether it is great value, a fair price or a high markup.
